# help dismissrcopyvv
dismissrcopyvv - Dismiss one or more virtual volumes from a remote copy group.

SYNTAX
    dismissrcopyvv [options] {<pattern> | <VV_name>} <group_name>
    dismissrcopyvv [options] {<set> | <pattern> } <group_name>

DESCRIPTION
    The dismissrcopyvv command removes a virtual volume from a remote copy volume
    group.

AUTHORITY
    Super, Edit
    Any role granted the rcopyvv_dismiss right

OPTIONS
    -f
        Does not ask for confirmation for the dismissrcopyvv command.

    -pat
        Specifies that specified patterns are treated as glob-style patterns
        and all remote copy volumes matching the specified pattern will be
        dismissed from the remote copy group. This option must be used
        if the <pattern> specifier is used.

    -keepsnap
        Specifies that the Primary volume's resync snapshot should be retained
        after the volumes are dismissed from the remote copy group.
        This snapshot will reflect the state of the secondary volume and can be
        used as the resync starting point if the volumes are re-admitted to a
        remote copy group. The snapshot's name will begin with "sv.rcpy.".
        For example, when dismissing a volume from a synchronous remote copy
        group, snaps are created for each volume (sv.rcpy.<volume-name>) of
        the set in the primary. Secondary volumes are still left intact in
        the secondary set but the secondary set is disassociated from the
        secondary RC group. This snapshot will be deleted automatically
        after the delta synchronization completes.

    -removevv
        secondary volumes are removed from secondary set and deleted.
        The secondary set is also removed when the last volume in the set
        is removed.

    -keepalua
        Keeps the local volume's ALUA state from changing. This option
        must be used during Peer Motion migrations of Remote Copy Groups.
        Please refer to "Volume migration in a Remote Copy Primary group"
        in the Peer Motion User Guide for further details.

SPECIFIERS
    <set>
       Name of the set of volumes dismissed from the RC group.

    <VV_name>
       The name of the volume to be removed. Volumes are added to a group
       with the admitrcopyvv command.

    <pattern>
       Specifies a glob-style pattern. This specifier can be repeated to dismiss
       multiple remote copy volumes. If this specifier is not used, the <VV_name>
       specifier must be used.

    <group_name>
        The name of the group that currently includes the virtual volume.

NOTES
    Access to all domains is required to run this command.

    The -keepsnap and -removevv options are mutually exclusive.

    The dismissrcopyvv command removes any Remote Copy synchronization snapshots
    affiliated with the removed volume.

    If a group's target has the mirror_config policy set and the group is
    a primary group, this command is mirrored to that target and the volume
    is removed from the corresponding secondary group. If the policy is set
    and the group is a secondary, this command fails.

    If the group's automatically created volume set was specified when its
    virtual volumes were created, i.e., "createvlun set:<RCP_group_name>...",
    then, when a volume is dismissed from the group, its VLUN will
    also be removed.

EXAMPLES
    The following example dismisses virtual volume vv1 from Group1:

        cli% dismissrcopyvv vv1 Group1

    The following example dismisses all virtual volumes that start with
    the name testvv from Group1:

        cli% dismissrcopyvv -pat testvv* Group1

    The following example dismisses volume vv1 from Group1 and removes the
    corresponding volumes of vv1 on all the target systems of Group1.

        cli% dismissrcopyvv -removevv vv1 Group1

    The following example dismisses volume vv2 from Group2 and retains the
    resync snapshot associated with vv2 for this group.

        cli% dismissrcopyvv -keepsnap vv2 Group2

    The following example dismisses all virtual volumes that are part of
    set (vvset1) from Group1.

        cli% dismissrcopyvv set:vvset1 Group1

    The following example dismisses all virtual volumes that start with
    the name testvv which are part of set (vvset1) from Group1:

        cli% dismissrcopyvv -pat set:vvset1:testvv* Group1
